plain: For most lakehouse architectures, Apache Parquet is the standard choice for storing raw and processed data, since it's a columnar format that compresses well and supports efficient analytical queries by letting engines read only the columns they need. On top of Parquet, table formats like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, or Apache Hudi add transaction support, schema evolution, time travel, and reliable upserts and deletes, which plain Parquet files alone can't do well. Delta Lake pairs naturally with Databricks, Iceberg has broad multi-engine support (Spark, Trino, Flink), and Hudi focuses on fast incremental upserts. Most modern lakehouses use Parquet plus one of these table formats together.
